abstracts.title: Knowledge graph-guided multiple sclerosis identification and therapeutic trend analysis: Real-world evidence from two large healthcare systems.
abstracts.abstract: The multiple sclerosis (MS) therapeutic landscape has evolved over time. We conducted a knowledge graph-guided analysis of MS-specific disease-modifying therapy (DMT) prescription trends using longitudinal real-world clinical data. We analyzed registry-linked electronic health record (EHR) data from two large independent healthcare systems between 2004 and 2022, including both academic and community practices. We developed an unsupervised phenotyping algorithm that leverages a publicly available knowledge graph and informative EHR features to identify patients with MS. After identifying MS cases, we combined the two cohorts and constructed annual time-varying knowledge graphs that capture co-occurrence patterns between DMTs and MS diagnosis. For each year, we analyzed co-occurrence patterns between DMTs and MS diagnosis using Shifted Positive Pointwise Mutual Information transformation and singular value decomposition to generate embeddings. We computed patient-wise cosine similarities and confidence intervals to quantify MS-specific DMT usage patterns. The phenotyping algorithm achieved robust performance in predicting MS diagnosis (AUROC: MGB = 0.994, UPMC = 0.922), identifying…

abstracts.title: No association between the wearing-off effect and α4-integrin receptor saturation in natalizumab treated patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.
abstracts.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
abstracts.abstract: Approximately half of patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis treated with natalizumab (NTZ) report transient symptom worsening - particularly fatigue - toward the end of the dosing interval. This phenomenon, commonly referred to as the wearing-off effect (WOE), has been hypothesized to result from a decrease in α4-integrin receptor saturation on circulating leucocytes. However, existing evidence is inconsistent, considering either small samples studied or conflicting results derived from previous studies. Our study aimed to investigate the association between α4-integrin receptor saturation and the WOE in a large prospective cohort of NTZ treated patients. We conducted a prospective observational study collecting demographic and clinical data, including WOE assessment via a structured questionnaire, treatment interval data, and α4-integrin receptor saturation levels across T-lymphocyte subset. Among 117 participants, 57.3 % reported experiencing WOE. WOE was significantly associated with higher disability (EDSS score) and longer NTZ treatment duration. However, no significant correlation was found between WOE and α4-integrin receptor saturation in any T-lymphocyte su…

abstracts.title: Blocking the microglia-endothelial axis via SPP1-ITGAV disruption attenuates neuroinflammation in multiple sclerosis.
abstracts.abstract: Background Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system (CNS) characterized by persistent neuroinflammation and immune cell infiltration. Despite extensive study, the specific mechanisms by which local microenvironmental signals enable peripheral immune cells to breach the blood-brain barrier (BBB)-especially without overt structural disruption-are not fully understood. Methods We utilized integrated transcriptomic analysis to identify specific microglia populations in demyelinating lesions. In vitro cellular models, coupled with confocal microscopy and biochemical analyses, were employed to investigate the interaction between microglia-derived factors and vascular endothelial cells, specifically evaluating adhesion molecule dynamics and transendothelial migration. In vivo validation was performed using an experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) mouse model to assess the effects of targeted pharmacological inhibition on immune cell infiltration and clinical disease severity. abstracts.title: Biological and clinical stability after switching from intravenous to subcutaneous natalizumab in RRMS under standard and extended dosing.
abstracts.abstract: Introduction Natalizumab (NTZ) is a high-efficacy therapy for relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) that can be administered intravenously (IV) or subcutaneously (SC). While switching from IV to SC NTZ is increasingly common in clinical practice, evidence on pharmacodynamic stability, particularly under extended interval dosing (6 weeks), remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate CD49d receptor occupancy (RO), serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL) levels, and clinical outcomes in RRMS patients switching from IV to SC NTZ while maintaining either 4- or 6-week dosing intervals. Methods We conducted a multicenter, ambispective, observational study including RRMS patients who had received IV NTZ for at least 6 months on a 4w or 6w schedule and subsequently switched to SC NTZ while maintaining the same dosing interval. CD49d RO was assessed in CD4+, CD8+, and CD19+ lymphocyte subsets before the first, third, and seventh SC administrations. sNfL levels and clinical outcomes (relapses, MRI activity, EDSS score) were also evaluated. Mixed models for repeated measures were applied. Results A total of 48 patients were included (4w: n=20; 6w: n=28). CD49d RO remained stable over…

abstracts.title: From Global Evidence to Saudi Practice: A Structured Evidence Map of the Diagnosis, Molecular Targets, and Therapeutic Strategies of Multiple Sclerosis in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
abstracts.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) has shifted in a generation from an uncommon diagnosis in Saudi Arabia to a major cause of neurological disability in young adults. Available Saudi data describe clinical characteristics broadly similar to those reported elsewhere in the Middle East and do not show that Saudi patients differ from trial populations, although this does not establish equivalent efficacy or safety. How far global advances are usable in the Kingdom has not, however, been synthesized. This narrative review maps diagnostic and therapeutic strategies across five separately reported domains (clinical evidence, 2022 national consensus listing, affordability, monitoring requirement, regional data), with categories assigned by a pre-specified rule, not a composite grade. Regional evidence on established therapies is entirely observational: cohorts report favourable outcomes with fingolimod, natalizumab, and off-label rituximab but cannot establish comparative effectiveness, and physicians report cost, availability, and insurance formularies as constraints whose extent has not been quantified. abstracts.title: Natalizumab exacerbates astrocytopathy in NMOSD via blockade of endothelial VCAM1-astrocytic integrin α4 interaction.
abstracts.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
abstracts.abstract: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is a rare autoimmune inflammatory disorder of the central nervous system (CNS) that shares clinical features with multiple sclerosis (MS) but typically manifests with more severe symptoms. The presence of pathogenic IgG autoantibodies targeting aquaporin-4 (AQP4) channels on astrocytes serves as a highly specific biomarker that distinguishes NMOSD from MS. Unlike MS, NMOSD is characterized by profound astrocytic destruction and exhibits a distinct response to therapies. Notably, disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) effective in MS, including natalizumab, interferon-β, and fingolimod, not only fail to benefit NMOSD patients but may also exacerbate disease progression. The precise molecular mechanisms underlying this immunomodulator-induced exacerbation, however, remain not yet fully elucidated. Here, we demonstrate that natalizumab alleviated experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) while exacerbating the autoimmune astrocytopathy in an "EAE-NMOSD" mouse model, a phenomenon associated with a reduction in actively proliferating astrocytes. Through molecular and signaling pathway analyses, we identify that endothelial-derived vascul…

abstracts.title: Dose Optimization of BIIB107, an Anti-Alpha-4 Integrin Monoclonal Antibody, Through Population Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Modeling.
abstracts.abstract: BIIB107 is a recombinant, humanized monoclonal antibody targeting α4 integrin receptors, exhibiting a high binding affinity and strong receptor engagement potential in preclinical models, designed to prevent lymphocyte trafficking in multiple sclerosis (MS). This study aimed to characterize its pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) relationship using model-based approaches to inform dose optimization. A Phase 1 study (NCT04593121) was conducted in 76 healthy volunteers who received single ascending doses intravenously or subcutaneously (SC), along with multiple ascending doses SC. Population PK and PK-PD models were developed to quantify BIIB107 disposition and its effect on α4 integrin receptor saturation. A sigmoidal Emax model was used to characterize the concentration-effect relationship, and Monte Carlo simulations assessed dosing strategies for sustained α4 integrin engagement. BIIB107 exhibited nonlinear, target-mediated clearance, best described by a two-compartment model with first-order absorption and Michaelis-Menten elimination. abstracts.title: Targeting the TL1A pathway in inflammatory bowel disease: mechanistic insights and emerging therapeutic pipeline.
abstracts.abstract: Tumor necrosis factor-like ligand 1A (TL1A), encoded by TNFSF15, signals through death receptor 3 on effector T cells, innate lymphoid cells, and intestinal myofibroblasts, driving both chronic intestinal inflammation and tissue fibrosis. In this narrative review, we provide a contemporary appraisal of TL1A-directed therapeutics in inflammatory bowel disease based on electronic searches through May 2026. Three anti-TL1A monoclonal antibodies (tulisokibart, afimkibart, and duvakitug) have advanced to phase 3 trials across multiple global programs, with phase 2 clinical remission rates of 26%-48% in ulcerative colitis (placebo-adjusted differences 15-26 percentage points) and endoscopic response rates of 26%-48% in Crohn's disease, alongside favorable safety profiles. Mucosal transcriptomic and serum proteomic analyses from phase 2 trials, including DDW 2026 readouts from ARTEMIS-UC and TUSCANY-2, provide the first human-tissue confirmation of class antifibrotic activity through the suppression of Th17, myeloid, and extracellular matrix pathways. TNFSF15 risk-variant companion diagnostics are advancing, although their incremental utility remains modest and will be definitively teste…

data.boxed_warning: WARNING: PROGRESSIVE MULTIFOCAL LEUKOENCEPHALOPATHY TYSABRI increases the risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), an opportunistic viral infection of the brain that usually leads to death or severe disability. Risk factors for the development of PML include the presence of anti-JCV antibodies, duration of therapy, and prior use of immunosuppressants. These factors should be considered in the context of expected benefit when initiating and continuing treatment with TYSABRI [ see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) ]. Healthcare professionals should monitor patients on TYSABRI for any new sign or symptom that may be suggestive of PML. TYSABRI dosing should be withheld immediately at the first sign or symptom suggestive of PML. For diagnosis, an evaluation that includes a gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan of the brain and, when indicated, cerebrospinal fluid analysis for JC viral DNA are recommended [ see Contraindications ( 4 ), Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) ]. Because of the risk of PML, TYSABRI is available only through a restricted program under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) called the TOUCH ® Prescribing Program [ see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 ) ]. data.warnings_and_cautions: 5 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS Herpes infections: Life-threatening and fatal cases have occurred with herpes encephalitis and meningitis infections. Blindness has occurred in patients developing acute retinal necrosis. Discontinue TYSABRI if these infections occur and treat appropriately ( 5.3 ) Hepatotoxicity: Significant liver injury, including liver failure requiring transplant, has occurred. Discontinue TYSABRI in patients with evidence of liver injury ( 5.4 ) Hypersensitivity reactions: Serious hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis) have occurred. Permanently discontinue TYSABRI if such a reaction occurs ( 5.5 ) Immunosuppression/Infections: TYSABRI may increase the risk for certain infections. Monitor patients for development of infections due to increased risk with use of TYSABRI ( 5.6 ) Hematological Abnormalities: TYSABRI may cause thrombocytopenia. Monitor patients for bleeding abnormalities. Discontinue TYSABRI in patients with thrombocytopenia. Neonatal thrombocytopenia and anemia have also occurred. Obtain a complete blood count in neonates exposed to TYSABRI in utero. Three anti-TL1A monoclonal antibodies (tulisokibart, afimkibart, and duvakitug) have advanced to phase 3 trials across multiple global programs, with phase 2 clinical remission rates of 26%-48% in ulcerative colitis (placebo-adjusted differences 15-26 percentage points) and endoscopic response rates of 26%-48% in Crohn's disease, alongside favorable safety profiles. Mucosal transcriptomic and serum proteomic analyses from phase 2 trials, including DDW 2026 readouts from ARTEMIS-UC and TUSCANY-2, provide the first human-tissue confirmation of class antifibrotic activity through the suppression of Th17, myeloid, and extracellular matrix pathways. Risk factors for the development of PML include the presence of anti-JCV antibodies, duration of therapy, and prior use of immunosuppressants. These factors should be considered in the context of expected benefit when initiating and continuing treatment with TYSABRI [ see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) ]. Healthcare professionals should monitor patients on TYSABRI for any new sign or symptom that may be suggestive of PML. TYSABRI dosing should be withheld immediately at the first sign or symptom suggestive of PML. For diagnosis, an evaluation that includes a gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan of the brain and, when indicated, cerebrospinal fluid analysis for JC viral DNA are recommended [ see Contraindications ( 4 ), Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) ]. Because of the risk of PML, TYSABRI is available only through a restricted program under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) called the TOUCH ® Prescribing Program [ see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 ) ]. abstracts.title: Emergence of natalizumab anti-drug antibodies during extended interval dosing in a patient with multiple sclerosis: A case report.
abstracts.abstract: Background We present a natalizumab-treated patient with multiple sclerosis (MS) who developed neutralizing anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) after years of treatment following introduction of extended interval dosing (EID). Objectives To gain insight into how this sudden ADA development occurred. Methods A pharmacokinetic model was used to evaluate the relation between natalizumab concentration and ADA production. Results EID from 4 to 6 weeks resulted in unexpectedly low natalizumab trough concentrations accompanied by increasing ADAs. Modeling suggested ADA production was stimulated by declining natalizumab concentrations. Conclusions EID may result in increased ADA production, causing ADA-mediated clearance of natalizumab and risking new MS activity.

abstracts.title: Lower recorded prevalence of Alzheimer's disease in natalizumab-exposed older adults with multiple sclerosis: A hypothesis-generating observation.
abstracts.abstract: Adaptive immune mechanisms, including CD8 T cell-mediated neuroinflammation, are increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease. We examined whether exposure to natalizumab, an α4-integrin antagonist that restricts leukocyte trafficking into the central nervous system, was associated with Alzheimer's disease prevalence among older adults with multiple sclerosis. Using Epic Cosmos electronic health record data, we identified 875,226 individuals with MS, of whom 9095 had an Alzheimer's disease diagnosis after age 65 years. Alzheimer's disease prevalence differed significantly across disease-modifying therapies, with natalizumab-treated patients demonstrating the lowest prevalence (0.13%; 95% confidence interval: 0.10-0.17%). These findings demonstrate a lower recorded prevalence of late-life Alzheimer's disease among natalizumab-exposed patients; however, given the aggregated nature of the data, this observation should be considered descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

abstracts.title: Lymphocytosis as a biomarker for natalizumab treatment response in multiple sclerosis: The link with anti-drug antibodies.
abstracts.abstract: Background Natalizumab is a high-efficacy therapy drug for multiple sclerosis that inhibits lymphocyte migration into the central nervous system, increasing lymphocyte counts in the peripheral blood. Anti-drug antibody responses may limit drug efficacy, but current guidance recommends anti-drug antibody testing only after evidence of 'reduced efficacy'. Objective To assess the lack of relative lymphocytosis as a biomarker of anti-drug antibody responses. Methods Lymphocyte counts and immunogenicity data from the pivotal AFFIRM clinical trial ( n = 627 natalizumab vs n = 315 placebo) and real-world data from the Cardiff MS register ( n = 185) were analysed to assess the relationship between lymphocyte counts, anti-drug antibody responses, drug levels and disease activity. Results Natalizumab treatment induced an absolute change in lymphocyte counts by week 12 (1.40 ± 0.92 vs -0.05 ± 0.62 × 10 9 cells/L in natalizumab vs placebo; p 9 cells/L). Increases in lymphocyte counts by ⩾ 0.8 × 10 9 cells/L from the baseline discriminated individuals without anti-drug antibody responses with high sensitivity (≥ 84%) and specificity (≥ 91%). abstracts.title: Multiple sclerosis relapse following gamma knife radiosurgery for meningioma in a patient treated with natalizumab: case report.
abstracts.abstract: Objectives We describe a case of a patient with multiple sclerosis (MS) stable on natalizumab who developed widespread gadolinium-enhancing lesions and clinical relapse seven and eight months after gamma knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for left cerebellar convexity meningioma. We explore how increased blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability post-GKRS could potentially interfere with the lymphocyte anti-trafficking effect of natalizumab and result in new central nervous system (CNS) inflammation distant from the radiation site. Methods Comprehensive analysis of the patient's chart, brain and spine imaging, serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) profiles was conducted. We compiled a graphical representation of treatment changes, radiologic findings, and GKRS initiation within one timeframe. We conducted a structured literature review to support the discussion of this case and hypothesize possible pathophysiological mechanisms contributing to clinical and radiological findings. abstracts.title: Long-term outcomes of alemtuzumab in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis: a real-world cohort with particular focus on treatment sequencing after natalizumab.
abstracts.abstract: Background The role of alemtuzumab (ALEM) after natalizumab (NTZ) discontinuation in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) remains to be better defined in real-world settings. Methods We conducted a retrospective, longitudinal, single-centre cohort study including RRMS patients treated with ALEM. Clinical and MRI evaluations were performed every 6 months. Annualized relapse rate (ARR), and radiological activity were assessed longitudinally. NEDA-3 was evaluated both as an annual interval-specific outcome and as sustained NEDA-3 using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Results Eighty-one patients were included, with a mean follow-up after alemtuzumab of 65 months. In this real-world cohort with long-term follow-up, alemtuzumab was associated with sustained control of inflammatory disease activity in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (mean annualized relapse rate of 0.069, mean annual NEDA-3 proportion of 80.7% from years 2 to 7), while and EDSS modest improvement at month 36 versus baseline (p = 0.04). abstracts.title: A Case of Treatment-Refractory Tumefactive Multiple Sclerosis Mimicking Brain Abscess.
abstracts.abstract: A 47-year-old female presented with one week of left facial numbness following recent dental extractions. Initial brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with and without contrast revealed a contrast-enhancing lesion in the right parieto-occipital lobe with mild diffusion restriction and surrounding vasogenic edema, as well as smaller enhancing lesions in the right frontal and parietal lobes. Empiric intravenous (IV) antibiotic treatment was started due to a high concern for odontogenic brain abscesses. Despite antibiotic treatment, repeat brain MRI revealed new contrast-enhancing lesions in the left pons and cerebellar peduncle, suggesting that infection was unlikely and antibiotics were discontinued. The differential diagnosis broadened to neoplastic, inflammatory, and demyelinating pathologies. A brain biopsy of the right occipital lobe lesion was pursued for a definitive diagnosis. Following the brain biopsy, the patient received five days of IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily, followed by a two-week oral prednisone taper with clinical improvement. abstracts.title: Proportionate and disproportionate reporting of different infectious complications of disease modifying therapy in multiple sclerosis.
abstracts.abstract: Introduction Progessive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) is a complication of immunoincompetence due to disease or immunosuppressive therapy and in particular due to disease modifying therapy (DMT) in multiple sclerosis. It is not clear however, whether there is a specific vulnerability to PML or whether this is due to immunosuppression per se. The same holds for the combination of cryptococcal disease and Fingolimod. Methods We used the reporting odds ratio (ROR) as calculated from entries to Vigibase for a sample of drugs used for DMT (Alemtuzumab, Cladribine, Fingolimod, Dimethyl fumarate, Glatirameracetat, Interferon beta-1a, Interferon beta-1b, Natalizumab, Ocrelizumab, Ofatumumab, Ozanimod, Peginterferon-beta-1a, Ponesimod, Siponimod, and Teriflunomide) and infections with the varicella zoster virus (VZV), PML, and cryptococcal and pneumococcal disease as a surrogate for the frequency of these events. Principal component analysis was used to identify outliers of the general relation between the RORs for the 4 infections studied. A plot of log(ROR) for the other infections as a function of log(ROR) of VZV infections was used to characterize the outliers more clearly. Resu…

Landscape: 31 trials in MS, per site_target; Biogen is dominant sponsor. 22 stopped or terminated, 19 completed. Key stop reasons: sponsor business decisions, lack of statistical significance (ASCEND study), slow enrollment. Mechanism: α4-integrin blockade to stop lymphocyte trafficking.

Track record: Natalizumab (TYSABRI) is approved for MS and Crohn's. ChEMBL call failed; FDA label confirms MS indication and black box warning for PML. No other drugs in class approved.

Literature: Recent PMIDs show ongoing research: anti-drug antibodies with extended dosing (PMID:42969026), lymphocytosis as biomarker (PMID:42891510), low Alzheimer's prevalence in natalizumab users (PMID:42978183), PML risk analysis (PMID:42907929). Also, natalizumab may worsen NMOSD (PMID:41671178).

Competition: No stop-risk from site_risk (unavailable). High PML risk is a known competitive liability. Natalizumab remains a high-efficacy option despite risk.

Key IDs: NCT05265728 (terminated), NCT03689972 (completed), FDA:c5fdde91-1989-4dd2-9129-4f3323ea2962, PMID:42969026, PMID:42891510, PMID:41671178.

sections.text: Thirty-one trials have tested α4-integrin blockade in multiple sclerosis, with Biogen as the lead sponsor in 26 of them.
Nine trials were terminated, including a Phase 3 study (NCT01416181) that did not achieve statistical significance on primary or secondary endpoints.
Natalizumab is approved for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis and acts by blocking α4-integrin to inhibit lymphocyte trafficking into the central nervous system.
Natalizumab carries a FDA boxed warning for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), a risk that increases with anti-JCV antibody status, treatment duration, and prior immunosuppressant use.
The risk of PML has led to restricted access via the TOUCH Prescribing Program, which limits broader use despite efficacy.
No other drugs in the α4-integrin inhibitor class have been approved for multiple sclerosis.
Recent observational data suggest that extended interval dosing of natalizumab may lead to low drug trough levels and emergence of neutralizing anti-drug antibodies, risking loss of efficacy.
Lack of expected lymphocytosis on treatment may serve as a biomarker for anti-drug antibody development.
Natalizumab may exacerbate neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder due to blockade of endothelial VCAM1-astrocytic integrin α4 interaction.
Real-world evidence indicates durable efficacy after switching to alemtuzumab post-natalizumab, suggesting established exit strategies from high-risk therapies.

read: Mechanism evidence: α4-integrin blockade remains a validated mechanism for reducing CNS inflammation in MS, but is limited by PML risk and immunogenicity concerns.
Competitive position: Natalizumab is a high-efficacy option with entrenched safety liabilities, facing competition from safer, high-efficacy alternatives.

Open questions: Can biomarker-guided monitoring (e.g., lymphocytosis, drug levels) mitigate immunogenicity and extend safe use? Does CNS immune restriction provide benefit in non-MS neurodegenerative conditions?
would_change: Evidence of successful biomarker-guided extended interval dosing maintaining receptor saturation without immunogenicity would favour continued investment.
Demonstration of benefit in progressive MS or other neuroinflammatory conditions could shift the risk-benefit balance.

FDA boxed warning confirms PML risk and lists anti-JCV antibodies, duration, prior immunosuppressants as risk factors.
FDA source mentions TOUCH Prescribing Program as restricted access due to PML risk.
Only natalizumab is listed in approved MS drugs in the α4-integrin chain from the source.
